subtitle: World Championship Grand Prix wins by driver, race by race, 2014 – 2021
notes: IQ-05 round 2 (DEC-027): the settings the round-2 pilots shared. Round 3 (DEC-034): Luke chose A (top 20) and variant B's config was deleted, so only config_pilot_2014_2021_top20.json extends this file now; the winner line stays a switch (winner_line.enabled). Not a pilot on its own.
The 160 races of 2014-2021 at 0.5 s per race (Luke: the pace is fine). The board opens on the totals before the 2014 opener.
Opening (blueprint section 12): no title card (intro_sec 0). The board, with the title and subtitle on it, is on screen from the first frame for pacing.lead_in_sec before the first race.
Ending: the final board is on screen for exactly pacing.final_board_sec (10 s, blueprint 8-12 s) from the first frame of the last race; no closing card (outro_sec 0).
pacing.judge_rows 10: the beat of every race is judged on the top ten in both variants, so A and B run on identical timestamps and can be compared frame for frame (blueprint section 9).

record_hold (a switchable test, blueprint section 11): races on which a driver equals (BECOMES_JOINT) or takes (BECOMES_SOLE) the all-time record, as in data/rtt-002/record_progression.csv, are held 2.0 s so the rank glide settles (1.5 s in round 2; lengthened in round 3, DEC-034 step 6). In 2014-2021: 2020 Eifel GP (Hamilton equals Schumacher's 91) and 2020 Portuguese GP (Hamilton 92, sole record). Set enabled to false to switch it off.

highlight (Luke: the winner's bar should flash; blueprint section 10: no flashes or strobing, one gentle highlight): the credited winner's bar, if it is on the board, is brightened 30% towards white with a soft glow on the first frame of the race and fades over 0.4 s; a driver who also wins the next race stays lit through the streak instead of fading and re-lighting.
